_meta.description: Mapping of finding types to DORA Chapter II (ICT risk management) articles. High value for UK financial services roles, since DORA applies to EU financial entities and their critical ICT third-party providers.
_meta.mapping_rationale: Article titles (Article 9 'Protection and prevention', Article 10 'Detection', Article 12 'Backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods') and the specific sub-paragraph quotes in audit_notes below were verified against DORA reference sources before this file was written, not generated from memory. EUR-Lex's own page for this regulation repeatedly truncated before reaching Chapter II in this session (a very long preamble precedes the articles), so sub-paragraph text was cross-checked against a secondary DORA reference site quoting the regulation article-by-article, rather than read directly off the Official Journal PDF. Article and paragraph numbers are accurate to that source; a human should spot-check the exact wording against the official Official Journal PDF before this mapping is relied on in front of a real auditor, the same caveat NIS2's mapping_rationale already carries for its own interpretive judgment calls.

audit_notes.S3_PUBLIC_VIA_ACL: Article 9(4)(c): 'implement access limitation policies restricting physical or logical access to necessary functions only'. An AllUsers ACL grant is the direct opposite of this.
audit_notes.S3_PUBLIC_VIA_AUTHENTICATED_USERS_ACL: Article 9(4)(c), reused. Same access-limitation failure, narrower audience -- still not limited to necessary functions.
audit_notes.S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCK_DISABLED: Article 9(4)(c), reused — PAB is exactly the access-limitation control this sub-paragraph describes, at the safety-net level rather than the individual-grant level.
audit_notes.S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED: Article 9(4)(d): 'implement policies and protocols for strong authentication mechanisms... and protection measures of cryptographic keys whereby data is encrypted'. Encryption at rest is the data-protection half of this sub-paragraph.
audit_notes.S3_ENCRYPTION_NOT_DEDICATED_KMS_KEY: Article 9(4)(d), reused — 'protection measures of cryptographic keys' names key management directly, which is exactly what this finding is about.
audit_notes.S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED: Article 12(1)(b): 'restoration and recovery procedures and methods'. Versioning is an object-level recovery mechanism.
audit_notes.S3_LOGGING_DISABLED: Article 10(3): entities must allocate 'sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity, the occurrence of ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents'. Access logs are the raw material this monitoring depends on.
audit_notes.S3_LIFECYCLE_MISSING: Article 12(1)(a): 'backup policies and procedures specifying the scope of the data that is subject to the backup and the minimum frequency'. A lifecycle policy is the retention-scope half of what this sub-paragraph requires be documented.
audit_notes.S3_LIFECYCLE_RULE_DISABLED: Article 12(1)(a), reused. A documented policy that isn't actually enforced (Status: Disabled) doesn't satisfy this sub-paragraph any more than having no policy at all.
audit_notes.S3_TLS_NOT_ENFORCED: Article 9(3)(a): ICT solutions must 'ensure the security of the means of transfer of data'. Deliberately mapped to a different sub-paragraph than S3_ENCRYPTION_DISABLED's 9(4)(d) — this one is specifically about data in transit, not at rest, and DORA's Article 9(3) addresses transfer security separately from Article 9(4)'s broader policy requirements.
audit_notes.KMS_KEY_ROTATION_DISABLED: Article 9(4)(d), reused — 'protection measures of cryptographic keys' names key management directly.
audit_notes.KMS_KEY_MISSING_ALIAS: Article 8(1), first use of this article in the file — DORA's general ICT asset identification duty ('identify, classify and adequately document all ICT... information assets and ICT assets'), a genuinely closer fit than stretching Article 9(4)(d)'s authentication/key-protection scope to cover asset labelling.
audit_notes.KMS_KEY_POLICY_OVERLY_BROAD: Article 9(4)(c), the same access-limitation reference used for the other 'more access than necessary' findings in this file. A wildcard key-policy principal is the clearest possible failure of 'access limitation... restricting access to necessary functions'.
audit_notes.KMS_KEY_PENDING_DELETION: Article 12(1)(b), reused from S3_VERSIONING_DISABLED — a completed key deletion is the permanent failure of restoration and recovery for everything that key protected.
audit_notes.IAM_ROOT_ACCESS_KEYS_ACTIVE: Article 9(4)(c), reused — root access keys are a standing credential with no restriction to necessary functions, the opposite of what this sub-paragraph requires.
audit_notes.IAM_ACCOUNT_MFA_NOT_ENABLED: Article 9(4)(d): 'strong authentication mechanisms, based on relevant standards'. Direct, unambiguous match.
audit_notes.IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY_WEAK: Article 9(4)(d), reused — password strength is part of the same authentication-mechanism requirement as MFA.
audit_notes.IAM_ACCESS_KEY_AGE_EXCEEDS_90_DAYS: Article 9(4)(c), reused — an unrotated, long-lived credential is a standing access grant that has outlived any 'necessary functions only' justification.
audit_notes.IAM_CONSOLE_LOGIN_ENABLED: Article 9(4)(c) reused a second time. A console login profile on a programmatic-only identity is an access method beyond what that identity's function requires — the same 'necessary functions only' test the access-key-age finding fails, applied to a different kind of excess access.
audit_notes.IAM_MULTIPLE_ACTIVE_ACCESS_KEYS: Article 9(4)(c) reused a third time. A second simultaneously-active credential is a second standing access grant beyond what's necessary at any given moment outside an active rotation.
audit_notes.ACCOUNT_CLOUDTRAIL_DISABLED: Article 10(3), reused from S3_LOGGING_DISABLED as the account-wide instance — CloudTrail is the primary mechanism for monitoring user activity and ICT anomalies across the whole account.
audit_notes.ACCOUNT_S3_BLOCK_PUBLIC_ACCESS_DISABLED: Article 9(4)(c), reused — the account-wide instance of the same access-limitation requirement as the bucket-level finding.
audit_notes.RESOURCE_MISSING_TAGS: Article 8(1), reused from KMS_KEY_MISSING_ALIAS — the same ICT asset identification duty, generalised across every taggable resource type instead of just KMS keys.
audit_notes.IAM_USER_ADMIN_POLICY_ATTACHED: Article 9(4)(c) reused a fourth time. Full administrative access on an identity is the opposite of restricting access to necessary functions — the clearest possible violation of this article's core requirement.
audit_notes.IAM_USER_POLICY_GRANTS_WILDCARD_ACTION: Article 9(4)(c), reused. Same access-limitation failure as IAM_USER_ADMIN_POLICY_ATTACHED, reached through a custom policy grant instead of the named AWS-managed one.
